name: Docker Containers
description: Containers on the host with logs, a shell, start, stop and restart; edit a container, create containers and stacks (a compose file, or one from a GitHub repository), and a Manage page for images, volumes and networks.
author: Bosun

permissions.label: See containers
permissions.description: See the Docker containers widget and the container list of a server.

permissions.label: View container logs
permissions.description: Read the recent log output of a container.

permissions.label: Start, stop and restart containers
permissions.description: Change the running state of containers on the host.

permissions.label: Open a shell in a container
permissions.description: Show the shell button on running containers (the web terminal needs Full access and your own login), and let an API key with this permission get a terminal in a container that cannot reach the host (the package checks this).

permissions.label: Create and change containers and stacks
permissions.description: Edit a container (it is replaced by a new one with the new settings), create containers, pull images and create volumes and networks, and deploy, change and restart stacks. Also lets you read the settings of a container, including its environment variables.

permissions.label: Use elevated container options
permissions.description: Set options that can give a container control over the host: privileged mode, host network or process namespace, extra capabilities, devices, security profiles, the Docker socket and sensitive host folders.

permissions.label: Remove containers, images, volumes, networks and stacks
permissions.description: Delete things from the host, including pruning unused images, volumes and networks.

widgets.description: Containers on the host with logs, a shell, edit, start, stop and restart; a Manage page and New container / New stack in the menu.

terminal.command: docker exec -it {{ref}} sh -c 'if command -v bash >/dev/null 2>&1; then exec bash; else exec sh; fi'

confirm.title: Restart {name}?
confirm.text: Anything the container is serving will be interrupted.

confirm.title: Stop {name}?
confirm.text: Anything the container is serving will be interrupted.

confirm.title: Replace the container?
confirm.text: The container is stopped and replaced by a new one with these settings. Its volumes are kept. If the new container cannot start, the old one is put back.

confirm.title: Replace the container with elevated options?
confirm.text: These options can give the container control over the host. The container is stopped and replaced by a new one; volumes are kept.

confirm.title: Remove {name}?
confirm.text: The container is stopped and deleted. Named volumes are kept.

confirm.title: Remove dangling images?
confirm.text: Only untagged leftovers of builds and pulls (<none>) are deleted. Images that have a name but no container stay: use "Remove all unused images" for those.

confirm.title: Remove all unused images?
confirm.text: Every image that no container uses is deleted, tagged or not, and has to be pulled again when it is needed. Images used by a stopped container are kept.

confirm.title: Remove volume {name}?
confirm.text: The data in the volume is deleted for good.

confirm.title: Remove unused volumes?
confirm.text: Every volume that no container uses is deleted, with its data.

confirm.title: Deploy with elevated options?
confirm.text: The stack may use privileged mode, the host network, devices, the Docker socket or host folders.

confirm.title: Remove stack {name}?
confirm.text: Its containers and networks are removed (volumes are kept).

edit.title: Edit {context.name}
edit.description: Saving replaces the running container with a new one that has these settings. Volumes are kept, and so are the settings this screen does not show. If the new container cannot start, the old one is put back.

blocks.text: This container already uses elevated options: {datasets.cur.risky_text}
Not shown here, but kept as they are: {datasets.cur.preserved_text}

fields.name: cmd
fields.label: Command (one argument per line)
fields.help: Leave empty to use the command of the image.

fields.name: port
fields.label: Published ports
fields.help: Which port of the host reaches which port of the container. "Publish all exposed ports" picks a free port on the host for every port the image declares; the ports are kept when you edit the container again.

fields.name: volume
fields.label: Volumes and folders
fields.help: A volume is storage Docker manages; a folder is a folder of the host shown inside the container. Read only keeps the container from changing it.

fields.name: env
fields.label: Environment variables
fields.help: Values of names such as PASSWORD or TOKEN are hidden and kept out of logs.

fields.label: Memory limit
fields.help: Empty: no limit.

fields.name: cpus
fields.label: CPU limit
fields.help: Number of CPUs. Empty: no limit.

fields.label: Privileged mode

fields.name: pid

fields.warn: The container can see and signal every process of the host.

fields.name: ipc
fields.label: IPC namespace
fields.warn: The container shares memory with host processes.

fields.name: cap_add
fields.label: Added capabilities
fields.warn: Extra capabilities can be used to escape the container.

fields.name: device

fields.warn: Host devices are handed to the container.

fields.name: security_opt

fields.warn: Disabling a security profile removes a protection of the container.

fields.name: sysctl
fields.label: Kernel parameters
fields.warn: Kernel parameters of the container can affect the host.

blocks.text: The settings of the container as they are now (saved ones, not what you are typing). They include its environment variables, so look before you share them.

stack_new.title: New stack
stack_new.description: A stack is a Docker Compose project: write the compose file here, or deploy one from a GitHub repository.

fields.label: Stack name
fields.help: Lowercase letters, digits, - and _.

fields.label: Repository (https)
fields.help: Private repository? An admin sets a GitHub access token under Settings, Widgets, Docker Containers (key icon).

fields.name: h_override
fields.label: Override settings of the compose file

fields.name: override
fields.label: Overrides
fields.help: Change a setting of one service without editing the repository: its container name, a port, a volume or its network. Ports, volumes and networks you list replace the ones of the compose file for that service. Needs Docker Compose 2.24 or newer.

fields.name: env
fields.label: Environment file (.env)
fields.help: Values of names such as PASSWORD or TOKEN are kept out of logs and saved encrypted.
